key_insight: SpyCAT uses a spatially context-aware transformer to model what normal brain MRI looks like, helping it spot subtle epileptogenic lesions as anomalies.
clinical_relevance: This approach may improve detection and localization of small, hard-to-see brain lesions in high-resolution MRI, which could support more accurate epilepsy workups.
method: Patch-based transformer over discrete tokens from a VQ-VAE
Uses 3D convolutions to generate counterfactual patches and encode spatial context
evidence_signal: In evaluations on point-annotated epileptogenic lesion subtypes, SpyCAT showed reliable lesion identification/localization and outperformed state-of-the-art reference methods.
watch_item: Results are based on annotated lesion subtypes in a specific MRI setting, so broader clinical generalization and workflow integration still need validation.
paper_title: Spatially Context-Aware Transformers Facilitate Modeling-Based Anomaly Detection of Subtle Lesions in Brain MRI Images
